title: How a freezer keeps food safe for months
examples: Why does frozen food last so long?

figure.name: x-why
figure.question: Why does frozen food last for months?
figure.answer: Frozen food is on pause: germs can't grow without liquid water.

because.label: Germs need water
because.note: Bacteria and moulds need liquid water to live and grow.

because.label: Water turns to ice
because.note: At −18 °C the water in food freezes solid.

because.label: Germs pause
because.note: With no liquid water and deep cold, germs stop growing.

because.label: Spoiling slows
because.note: Slow changes that spoil food almost stop.

explain.say: Ice cream, frozen peas and fish fingers can stay good for months in the freezer. How does that work? Look at the drop. Bacteria and moulds, the tiny living things that make food go bad, need liquid water to live and grow.

explain.say: Look at the moving dots on the board. They are water particles. As they get colder, they slow down and lock together into ice. Once they're locked, germs can't use them. Do you think the germs wake up again when the food thaws?

Yes, they do, so thawed food should be kept cold and eaten soon. Well done! Wow: Clarence Birdseye made frozen food popular in the 1920s, after he saw Inuit fishermen in Canada freeze fish in icy air, and it still tasted fresh months later!

faq.a: Like all living things, bacteria and moulds need liquid water to take in food and grow. When the water is frozen, they can't use it.
asks: What do germs need to grow?

faq.a: Mostly no. Freezing pauses germs; when food thaws, they can start growing again. Cooking food properly is what kills them.
asks: Do germs die in the freezer?

faq.q: How long can food stay in the freezer?
faq.a: At minus 18 degrees food stays safe for a long time, but its taste and texture slowly get worse. Many foods are best eaten within a few months.
Dry, pale patches where ice has slowly escaped from the surface of badly wrapped food. It is safe to eat but tastes dry.
asks: Why does frozen food get dry patches?

faq.a: People in cold places have frozen food for thousands of years. Clarence Birdseye made quick-frozen food popular in the 1920s, after learning from Inuit fishermen in Canada.
asks: Who made the first frozen food?

facts: Most home freezers are set to about −18 °C.
Freezing stops bacteria from growing but does not kill most of them.
